title: Three-dimensional implicit power-law creep relaxation and restart
purpose: Verify that backward-Euler material integration, the analytical algorithmic tangent, shared quadrature transaction, global Newton equilibrium, physical-time cutback, dissipation history, and checkpoint restoration operate as one finite-element procedure.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain isotropic Mises power-law creep

execution.evidence: A homogeneous constant-total-strain bar is compared with the analytical stress-relaxation solution; uninterrupted and restarted paths must recover identical displacement, CE, CEEQ, stress, accepted times, and dissipation history.

observables: The mean axial stress decays from the instantaneous elastic value toward the analytical power-law relaxation curve.
Equivalent creep strain and cumulative creep dissipation are positive and monotone.
An excessive equivalent creep-strain increment rejects an otherwise converged global attempt and causes atomic rollback and cutback.
Restart at physical time 5 reproduces the uninterrupted state at physical time 10.
acceptance: The analytical tangent matches a centered directional derivative of the backward-Euler update.
The ten-increment FE stress is within the declared time-discretization tolerance of the closed-form continuous-time relaxation solution.
Restart differences satisfy the strict automated floating-point tolerances.
Every accepted increment respects maximum_inelastic_increment when that control is active.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress
quantities.description: Backward-Euler ten-increment result for E=200000, nu=0.3, total axial strain 0.002, A=1e-6, n=3, reference stress 100, and duration 10.

quantities.name: mean_equivalent_creep_strain
quantities.description: Mean committed CEEQ for the same homogeneous relaxation path.

quantities.name: creep_dissipation
quantities.description: Accumulated stress-work conjugate to accepted creep-strain increments.

limitations: This homogeneous bar is an analytical and regression benchmark, not external component validation.
This benchmark is isothermal; the global provider is serial, single-material, small-strain, and three-dimensional.
The checkpoint requires the same serial mesh and degree-of-freedom layout.
Kachanov-Rabotnov damage and Sinh flow are not consumed by this global driver; Arrhenius field consumption has a separate regression.
